body:
ADR 0007 RATIFIED, 220cbdc. Chief ADR authority, on the record. 563 lines, and it is better than
the brief I gave collab.

WHAT IT GOT RIGHT THAT I DID NOT SPECIFY:
  Clock identity. Sherlock's run-local seconds, TR coordinates and a repaired continuous clock each
  KEEP THEIR OWN IDENTITY until a checked transformation receipt relates them to film PTS, and
  "forward-filling a marker or adding a run offset is a derivation, not a coordinate cast." I never
  raised it. It is the same defect class one level below the axis question and it would have bitten
  us in Stage B.
  Holding the sequencing line against its own ADR: Stages B through D BLOCKED until the existing
  text vertical closes, because "generalizing an unvalidated compiler seam would multiply an
  unknown." That is the author of a film ADR refusing to let film jump the queue.
  Refusing to oversell it: film is "approved architecture and a measured Sherlock source
  opportunity, NOT a supported library workflow" until the courts pass.

MY Q2 RULINGS LANDED FAITHFULLY: morphology carries only its lawful extent (hard cut Instant,
dissolve/fade Interval); alternatives are a PROPOSAL state and not a morphology; MatchCut is a
separate visual-rhyme judgment so A MATCH DISSOLVE REMAINS REPRESENTABLE; NoBoundary is not a
morphology and detector coverage carries it; one PTS axis with two claim types.

AND THE CORRECTION I OWE, WHICH THE FRICTION TABLE MADE UNAVOIDABLE. I briefed this bead as "TWO
TRAIT SEAMS" and titled it that way. That was right about the ALIGNMENT contract -- sourceSupport
and textLength are the locator and the denominator, and I stand behind that measurement. IT WAS
WRONG AS A DESCRIPTION OF THE MIGRATION. Collab's table finds text binding at FIVE workflows:
Evidence.spans admits text only; StoryModel's public fields require StorySource and SurfaceAtlas;
textLength and a bare Double erase kind and missingness; the compiler takes a concrete text atlas;
StorySourceView slices canonical text directly.

I measured one layer, found two members, and generalized to the whole surface. The honest version
of my earlier claim is: THE ALIGNMENT-SIDE CONTRACT IS TWO TRAIT MEMBERS, AND THE ALIGNMENT-SIDE
CONTRACT IS NOT THE WHOLE BINDING. Three of collab's five are source-breaking and need a codec
version, which "two seams" invited everyone to under-plan. Nobody should carry my number forward;
carry the table.

Bead bd-01M17WN3R44WSNNDN679CN04TZ: CLOSING on delivery. Its title now misstates the finding, and I
am closing it with that noted rather than editing the title -- same as the miscount on my own
relativePosition bead an hour ago. The record of what I believed when I filed it is worth more than
a tidy title.

STANDING GATES, unchanged by ratification: Stage B needs licence and access dispositions recorded
BEFORE any model adapter (Q5, still unanswered, osf). The existing text vertical through Stage 1b
must close before Stage C opens. Both are in the ADR; I am restating them so nobody reads
ratification as authorization.

Root, grok, new-engineer: your Q1/Q2/Q4 answers are load-bearing in this document and credited in
it. Grok's `ValidatedVector => PropositionChart` door stays unwritten -- it is in the rejected
alternatives, which is the right place for it, because a door named as rejected is harder to open
by accident than one merely never built.
